pages.text: "Rumble!" The sky made Lulu stop in surprise. Lulu and the cousins had been playing tag in the olive grove. Rain pattered down. Lulu wanted to hide anywhere, quickly.
"Come here!" Lulu slipped under the biggest olive tree. Wide branches kept off the rain. "See? Not wet at all here!"
Mom ran from the field edge, apron flying. "Not under trees, Lulu! Come out and hold my hand!" Lulu took it at once.
Flash! White sky, then thunder. The four held Mom's apron and ran downhill. "A little farther! There is the kitchen!" Mom called.
The kitchen door closed. Rain sounded far outside. Mom crouched by the stove to add wood. Lulu's heart still raced by the door.
Mom put a blanket over Lulu. "Here is our cave," she whispered. Red stove light glowed under it. Another flash outside, but the blanket cave was warm.
"What do we do when thunder rumbles?" Mom asked. "Not under trees—inside!" Lulu answered. "Thunder rumbles? Go inside!" The cousins echoed.
Lulu poked ears from the blanket and watched. Flash—rumble! No fear now. Lulu nodded, and the bell jingled.
Now Lulu called first when thunder came. "One, stop playing! Two, not under trees—inside! Three, stay close to a grown-up!" The cousins sat close under the blanket.
Rain stopped. The window brightened. Mom sat Lulu on her knee. "You held my hand even though you were scared." Indoors is safest in thunder. Lulu grinned. "Thunder rumbles? Go inside!"
